title: Targeting NLRP3 and AIM2 signaling pathways by Viscosol alleviates metabolic dysregulations induced inflammatory responses in diabetic neuro- and nephropathy: An in silico and in vivo study.
authors: Thahiem, Summan; Ihsan, Muhammad; Muneer, Hamza; Sohail, Aamir; Khan, Mehmand; Murtaza, Iram; Uddin, Zia; Shafique, Muhammad; Alzahrani, Khalid J; Ali, Hamid; Ullah, Imran
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和动物实验评估Viscosol对PTP1B/NLRP3/AIM2的抑制及糖尿病炎症缓解作用，对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) is a chronic metabolic disorder, considered the fastest growing pandemic of the 21stcentury. Meta-inflammation is a pivotal characteristic of T2D. Hyperactivated PTP1B, NLRP3, and AIM2 inflammasomes are considered the major regulators of metabolic inflammation. The concept of diabetes as an inflammatory disease has changed the pathogenic vision of T2D and hence, the compounds that mitigateinflammation in the setting of T2D are under the limelight of research. Current study aimed to evaluatethe anti-inflammatory potency of Viscosol, a novel PTP1B inhibitor, isolated from Dodonaea viscosa, in the STZ-HFD-induced T2D mouse model. Herein, male mice(C57BL/6), were administrated with Streptozotocin (STZ) (40mg/kg) and Viscosol (33mg/kg), intraperitoneally. Computational profiling revealed good absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) properties, least toxicity, and high docking score of Viscosol with PTP1B(-6.4 kcal/mol), NLRP3(-7.2 kcal/mol), and AIM2(-7.4 kcal/mol). Viscosol treatment significantly restored normal body weight (p < 0.0001), decreased the blood glucose level (p < 0.001), serum ROS level(p < 0.05) and diminished the severity of histopathological lesions, inflammatory lobules and increased the cell count of both brain and kidney tissues. The RT-qPCR analysis showed that Viscosol significantly reduced the mRNA expression of PTP1B, NF-kappaB, NLRP3, and AIM2up to 2.7-folds, 2.6-folds, 5.7-folds and 14.2-folds in the kidney tissues and 1.6-folds, 1.2-folds, 10.2-folds and 1.5-folds in brain tissues. Conclusively, inhibition of PTP1B via Viscosol could attenuate meta-inflammation by suppressing the aberrant NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasome signaling in diabetes-linked pathophysiology.
abstract_zh: 2型糖尿病（T2D）是一种慢性代谢性疾病，被认为是21世纪增长最快的大流行病。代谢性炎症（Meta-inflammation）是T2D的一个关键特征。过度激活的PTP1B、NLRP3和AIM2炎症小体被认为是代谢性炎症的主要调节因子。将糖尿病视为炎症性疾病的概念改变了T2D的病理学视角，因此，在T2D背景下减轻炎症的化合物成为研究焦点。本研究旨在评估Viscosol（一种从Dodonaea viscosa中分离的新型PTP1B抑制剂）在STZ-HFD诱导的T2D小鼠模型中的抗炎效力。在此，雄性小鼠（C57BL/6）通过腹腔注射给予链脲佐菌素（STZ）（40mg/kg）和Viscosol（33mg/kg）。计算分析显示，Viscosol具有良好的吸收、分布、代谢和排泄（ADME）特性，毒性最低，且与PTP1B（-6.4 kcal/mol）、NLRP3（-7.2 kcal/mol）和AIM2（-7.4 kcal/mol）具有高对接分数。Viscosol治疗显著恢复了正常体重（p < 0.0001），降低了血糖水平（p < 0.001）、血清ROS水平（p < 0.05），并减轻了组织病理学病变的严重程度、炎症小叶，同时增加了脑和肾组织的细胞计数。RT-qPCR分析显示，Viscosol显著降低了肾组织中PTP1B、NF-kappaB、NLRP3和AIM2的mRNA表达，分别降低至2.7倍、2.6倍、5.7倍和14.2倍，在脑组织中分别降低至1.6倍、1.2倍、10.2倍和1.5倍。总之，通过Viscosol抑制PTP1B可通过抑制糖尿病相关病理生理中异常的NLRP3和AIM2炎症小体信号传导来减轻代谢性炎症。
